I couldn't determine the root cause because every command I tried was denied. The session is in "don't ask" mode, and the Bash tool rejected all three of my read-only `kubectl` calls:

1. `kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide -l app=ledger-api` (to see which pods are NotReady)
2. `kubectl -n ledger get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp` (to see probe failures, OOMKills, or scheduling events)
3. `kubectl -n ledger rollout history deployment/ledger-api` (to confirm the 1.4.2 revision)

I have no other tool that can reach the cluster, and I won't try to get around the denial. Nothing has been checked yet, so I have no root cause, no supporting evidence, and nothing ruled out.

To continue, you could either:
- Allow Bash for read-only kubectl and promq in this session, then I'll rerun the checks above. Next I'd look at the NotReady pods' `describe` output and logs, the readiness probe config in the 1.4.2 pod spec compared with the previous revision, and the error-rate or latency metrics around the rollout time.
- Run those three commands yourself and paste the output here. The pod status, events, and the 1.4.2 change (probe settings, env/config, resource limits, or image changes) are usually enough to identify the cause.

steps.input: kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide -l app=ledger-api 2>/dev/null || kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide
